project.name: dklao
project.description: DK LAO Website 2026 — a Next.js 16 + Payload CMS corporate website and lead-generation platform for DK LAO, an industrial equipment partner in Laos (forklift rental and sales, spare parts, maintenance, warehouse solutions, cleaning equipment), including a quote-request lead pipeline and a mobile web app.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README, which describes DK LAO Website 2026: the brand positioning of DK LAO as an industrial equipment partner in Laos, the site's objectives, its user journeys, and the planned stack, routes and design direction. The root AGENTS.md bridge sits beside it and points contributors (including AI agents) to the con_agents governance package, which holds the repository, branch, quality-gate and footer-version rules. Together they explain what the site is for and the rules it is built under.

tour.title: Toolchain and Runtime Config
tour.description: package.json defines the pnpm scripts for Next.js dev, build and start, plus lint, typecheck, Vitest, version and link checks and the Payload CMS commands. tsconfig.json sets up strict TypeScript and the @/* and @payload-config path aliases used everywhere, and next.config.ts wraps Next.js with Payload's withPayload while applying the site-wide security headers from security-headers.ts. Knowing these files first makes the imports and behaviour in later steps easier to follow.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript path aliases in tsconfig.json ("paths": {"@/*": ["./src/*"]}) replace long relative imports like ../../lib/utils with @/lib/utils. The bundler and Vitest must be given the same aliases, which is why vitest.config.ts repeats them.

tour.title: Public Site Shell
tour.description: The (site) route group is the public website. Its layout.tsx defines the global metadata (title template, favicons, Open Graph, robots), imports globals.css, where the DK LAO design tokens such as navy, brand blue, action red and card radii are mapped into Tailwind, and mounts site-wide behaviour like GSAP motion. page.tsx then composes the homepage from a stack of sections: hero, proof facts, quick quote, solutions, rental, categories, forklift anatomy, industries, knowledge and the quote form.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router route groups use parentheses, as in (site), (app) and (payload). They organise folders and let each group have its own root layout without adding a segment to the URL, so /about lives at src/app/(site)/about/page.tsx.

tour.title: Content as Single Source
tour.description: The homepage does not hard-code its copy. It reads from static content modules in src/lib/data, which this project treats as the single source of truth. site-facts.ts holds owner-confirmed business facts (phone, WhatsApp, address, hours, reference clients), where a null value hides an unconfirmed item, and homepage.ts defines the CTAs, feature cards and categories. confirm.ts guards against planning text marked with [CONFIRM] reaching the public site, which follows the rule of no fake pricing, stock or claims.

tour.title: Route Registry and Page Model
tour.description: routes.ts and pages.ts are the most depended-on files in the codebase. routes.ts is the single route registry: header, footer, sitemap and related links all come from it, along with publish flags, breadcrumbs and per-page quote intents. pages.ts defines the PageContent model with typed sections, items and details, and filters out unconfirmed or fact-bound content. sitemap-pages.ts supplies built-in content for the 21 sitemap pages in that shape, and sitemap.ts advertises only published routes.

tour.title: Rendering Content Pages
tour.description: With the page model from Step 5 in place, a single generic ContentPage component renders the header, breadcrumb, hero, typed sections (cards, lists, chips, steps, FAQ accordions) and closing CTA for any PageContent. The catch-all [...slug] route uses it for every published sitemap page that has no route file of its own, preferring CMS content and returning 404 for unknown paths. Dedicated routes such as /forklift-rental reuse the same shell, so adding a page is mostly a data change.

tour.title: UI Component System
tour.description: Pages are assembled from a small design system. section.tsx provides the Container, Section, Eyebrow and SectionHeader primitives, button.tsx defines the DK LAO variants with class-variance-authority, and utils.ts exports the cn() helper used by almost every component to merge Tailwind classes. Marketing building blocks such as ServiceCard and the shared CTA band sit on top of these primitives, which keeps every page visually consistent.
tour.languageLesson: class-variance-authority (cva) declares a component's style variants as data, for example variant: {primary, secondary} and size: {sm, lg}, and returns a function that builds the matching class string. Combined with cn() (clsx plus tailwind-merge), callers can override classes without duplicate Tailwind utilities conflicting.

tour.title: Header, Navigation and Footer
tour.description: The site chrome is made of async server components. SiteHeader loads navigation (from the CMS when enabled) and renders the logo, the Radix-based desktop mega menu and the mobile drawer. IndustrialFooter builds contact chips, social marks and route groups. Its ownership line comes from site-metadata.ts, which reads the version from VERSION.json so the visible footer version never goes stale, as the governance rules require.

tour.title: Payload CMS Backend
tour.description: Payload CMS 3 runs inside the same Next.js app, a choice explained in the CMS backend decision record. payload.config.ts registers the Users, Pages, Articles and Leads collections plus the SiteFacts and Navigation globals on a Postgres adapter. access.ts defines the owner, editor and advisor roles that gate every collection. The pages collection mirrors the PageContent shape from Step 5, so CMS rows and built-in data stay interchangeable.

tour.title: CMS Loaders and Fallbacks
tour.description: The site keeps working without a database. client.ts reports whether the CMS is enabled (DATABASE_URL set) and lazily loads Payload. Loaders such as cms/pages.ts and cms/site-facts.ts map CMS rows to the site's types, validate section kinds and [CONFIRM] markers, and fall back to the built-in data from Steps 4 and 5 when the CMS is off. The Payload admin and REST API are exposed through catch-all routes in the (payload) group.

tour.title: Database Migrations
tour.description: The Postgres schema evolves through reviewed Payload migrations registered in order in migrations/index.ts. The initial migration creates users, leads and the site_facts global, and later migrations add pages, articles, navigation and card sections. A hand-written Supabase lockdown helper revokes public-schema privileges and enables row level security, and it is re-applied after migrations that add tables.
tour.languageLesson: Migrations are ordered, versioned schema changes with up and down steps, so every environment can reach the same database state reproducibly. Idempotent helpers, such as a lockdown that is safe to re-run, keep repeated or reordered runs from breaking.

tour.title: Quote Request Lead Pipeline
tour.description: Lead generation is the site's core business function. The client QuoteRequestForm validates input with the shared Zod quoteRequestSchema and posts to /api/leads/quote. That route rate-limits by client address, caps the body size, silently absorbs honeypot bot submissions, and validates again on the server. intents.ts maps ?category= keys to lead types, so every page's Request a Quote link preselects the right category.
tour.languageLesson: Defining one Zod schema and inferring TypeScript types from it (z.infer<typeof schema>) gives a single contract that validates the form on the client and the request on the server. This avoids client and server rules drifting apart.

tour.title: Lead Storage and Notifications
tour.description: After validation, store.ts saves the lead to the Payload leads collection (auto-generated DKL- IDs, access limited to owner and advisor) when a database is configured, and falls back to an append-only local JSONL file otherwise. The team is then notified by SMTP email and an optional HTTPS webhook with HMAC signing, which can feed Make, n8n, Zapier or WhatsApp gateways. This facade design means a lead is never lost just because the database is unavailable.

tour.title: Installable Mobile Web App
tour.description: The (app) route group is a separate installable PWA at /app, with its own root layout, an iOS- and Android-aware stylesheet and a web manifest. Its screens (home, services, request, location) reuse the same site facts and the Zod lead schema from earlier steps, and the RequestForm saves drafts locally. A service worker serves an offline fallback page that still offers a phone call link.
tour.languageLesson: A service worker is a background script that intercepts fetches. A network-first strategy tries the network and falls back to the cache, which keeps content fresh while still providing an offline page when there is no connection.

tour.title: Testing, CI and Deployment
tour.description: Vitest suites check content rules, the CMS, the lead pipeline and the production server; server.test.ts starts server.mjs both directly and through the cPanel Passenger entry app.js. The GitHub Actions CI workflow runs the version check, tests, lint, typecheck and build on pull requests and pushes. The deploy checklist describes running the built app as a systemd service behind an Apache proxy on DK LAO's cPanel server.
tour.languageLesson: In a GitHub Actions workflow, `on` sets the triggers (pull_request, push to chosen branches), `jobs` run in parallel by default, and the `steps` inside a job run in order. The quality gates are listed as sequential steps so that any failure stops the pipeline.
